description: Detect load anomalies from a pipeline audit log. For each monitored table and each calendar date between its first and last load_date, report at most one issue with this priority: (1) 'missing_load' when no audit row exists for the date; (2) 'volume_drop' when row_count < min_volume_ratio * baseline_avg, where baseline_avg is the average row_count of up to 7 previous loads of the table (existing rows only, current load excluded; no check when there is no previous load); (3) 'stale_data' when the hours between max_event_ts and the end of the load date (midnight following load_date, UTC) exceed max_lag_hours. Dates without an issue are not returned. Output columns: table_name (STRING), load_date (DATE), issue_type (STRING), row_count (INT64), baseline_avg (FLOAT64, 1 decimal). Sort by table_name, load_date.

load_date.description: Logical load date; at most one row per table per date

max_event_ts.description: Latest event timestamp contained in the load (UTC)

max_lag_hours.description: Maximum acceptable data lag in hours

edge_cases: 2025-06-05 has no audit row at all; it can only be found with a generated date spine
The baseline for 2025-06-06 includes the anomalous 400 (average 850) and excludes the current load
The first load of a table has no baseline and cannot be a volume_drop
common_failure_modes: FM7: Checking only existing audit rows can never detect a missing load
FM3: Window frame that includes the current row (ROWS BETWEEN 7 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) dilutes the baseline with the anomaly itself
FM2: Measuring lag against CURRENT_TIMESTAMP() or the start of load_date instead of the end of load_date makes results non-reproducible or off by 24 hours
